title: Ephemeral rate redispatch: burst smoothing and invoice volatility reduction
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Customers with bursty, short-lived traffic see large invoice spikes and a high proportion of late-arriving tokens that require manual adjudication. Existing reconciliation jobs are robust but operate at coarse windows and create noisy billing artifacts that increase support load and customer dissatisfaction.

Goal: Implement a lightweight, idempotent "ephemeral rate redispatch" worker that ingests raw usage events and performs tenant-aware temporal redistribution of token charges to smooth minute-level volatility while preserving a complete audit trail for downstream reconciliation and legal records. The worker should be able to: 1) apply configurable smoothing policies per-tenant (window, decay, hard caps), 2) reassign late-arriving tokens into the windowed ledger with confidence scoring, 3) emit explainable provenance for each redistributed token so downstream billing and dispute handlers can trace origin, and 4) operate with strong idempotency and backpressure controls to avoid creating double charges during retries.

Non-goals: This ticket does not change pricing tiers, does not attempt to do complex cross-tenant crediting, and does not replace the canonical reconciliation service — it augments the ingestion layer with proactive redistribution to reduce downstream churn and support tickets.
acceptance_criteria: Worker runs as a horizontally scalable k8s deployment and consumes raw usage Kafka topic with >99.9% availability in synthetic load tests
Redispatch decisions are persisted to the ledger via idempotent writes and produce no duplicate token records in acceptance test runs
Percentile invoice volatility (stddev of per-minute token charge at tenant-level) reduced by >=60% in canary tenants compared to baseline
All redispatched tokens include provenance fields (original_event_id, original_timestamp, redistribution_reason, confidence_score) visible in the ledger and audit UI
Comprehensive golden signals (redispatch-rate, pushed-back-pressure, idempotent-write-failures) saturate alerts and on-call runbook updated
Rollout plan (canary -> progressive -> global) validated with rollback toggle and documented in Confluence
implementation_notes: Design a compact redistribution model: sliding-window + exponential decay + tenant cap; parameters configurable in tenant profile store
Worker will first compute tentative redispatch map in-memory, then emit a batched idempotent write to 'ledger-redispatch' topic; separate compensator will reconcile any late diffs
Use a monotonic event fingerprint (source_stream, event_offset, sha256) to ensure idempotency across retries
Expose per-tenant debug mode that emits sample decisions to a secured debug topic for product and support triage
Integrate with existing billing-trace header so downstream stack (console, support tooling) can surface redistribution metadata
Trade-offs: smoothing reduces invoice volatility at the cost of temporal precision; we will default to conservative parameters for enterprise tenants and allow opt-out for strict accounting customers
comments: 2026-02-20 - Maya Chen: Initial triage and impact analysis. Collected sample tenant traces showing 3x minute-level spikes causing most disputes. Created design sketch and proposed sliding-window approach. Confluence draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/METER/Ephemeral+Redispatch+Design

2026-02-25 - Diego Martinez: Design review with billing and legal. Legal asked for immutable provenance for every redistributed token; added 'original_event_id' and 'redistribution_reason' fields. PM asked that enterprise tenants default to conservative smoothing (0-10% of burst redistributed).

2026-03-02 - Diego Martinez: Prototype worker implemented consuming 'usage-raw-v2' topic. End-to-end local test with synthetic bursts passes idempotency checks. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/usage-pipeline/pull/987

2026-03-06 - QA (Nina Gupta): Canary test plan added; will run against 5 low-risk tenants for 48 hours with debug logging enabled. Dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/usage/ephemeral-redispatch-canary

2026-03-10 - Diego Martinez: Canary started. Early telemetry shows redispatch rate ~8% and minute-level variance down by ~58% for canary tenants. Observed a 0.1% increase in idempotent-write retries due to transient db leader failovers; mitigated with backoff and leader pinning fix in PR #999.

2026-03-12 - Maya Chen: Stakeholder sync. Support estimates support-ticket volume reduction potential ~30% if canary trends hold. Preparing rollout playbook and runbook. Targeting progressive rollout next week with monitoring thresholds defined.
